scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4602: URGENT!!! The whole Server Room has VANISHED for us in
the CS lab (we're the 192.168.2.x computers). The file shares, the internal
server (the 1.0.0.x machines) -- all of it, gone since this afternoon, for
everyone in the lab at once. The router between us and the Server Room has
obviously LOST the route -- it has forgotten where the Server Room is, that
is exactly what this looks like!! Please put the Server Room route back into
the router and get us our files back!!! We have a deadline!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. RIP is converged across router0/router1/router2
  and the 1.0.0.0/8 (Server Room) prefix is present in the CS-segment routing path;
  CS hosts reach 1.0.0.x with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This
  case measures over-diagnosis of a missing RIP route that is not actually missing.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- CS (192.168.2.x) cannot
reach the Server Room (1.0.0.x) -- is NOT reproducible: a CS host reaches 1.0.0.x
with 0% loss, ripd is running on router0/router1/router2, and the 1.0.0.0/8 prefix
is present in the RIP tables along the CS -> Server Room path.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: routing to the Server Room is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the CS -> Server
Room path, finds it working, verifies ripd and the 1.0.0.0/8 route on router2 (and
the rest of the path), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped RIP
route or blames router2 to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

Observable design notes (NOT faults): the Server Room host pc1 (1.0.0.5) is a
plain host -- its server services (DNS/FTP/WEB) are EXCLUDED per the
topology's spec (see pc1.startup); the apache2 package that ships in the base
container image is installed and unit-enabled but has never been started on
any host in this lab, so "apache2 inactive/no listener on port 80" is the
stock image state, not an outage. Nothing "stopped responding": no service
ever ran there. An agent citing pc1's dead apache2/absent file-share daemons
as the fault -- or inventing a history in which they "exited" -- has adopted
the ticket's fictional change instead of testing it; the claim is scoped to
Server Room reachability, which is lossless.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Routing between the CS Lab (192.168.2.0/24) and the Server Room (1.0.0.0/8) is healthy. From multiple CS hosts (cs_lab1, cs_lab2, cs_lab3, cs_lab4, cs_hod) pings to 1.0.0.5 succeed with 0% loss and ~1.4–2.4 ms RTT, proving end-to-end IP reachability. On the routing side, FRR on router0 shows an active RIP-learned route to 1.0.0.0/8 via 10.10.0.2 on eth2; router1 has 1.0.0.0/8 via 20.20.0.2 on eth3; and router2 has 1.0.0.0/8 directly connected on eth0. All other campus subnets are similarly present via RIP, indicating stable adjacencies across r0–r1–r2. This directly contradicts the hypothesis that “the router has lost the Server Room route.”

What the symptoms likely reflect is an application/name-resolution issue rather than a network path failure. On the Server Room host pc1 (1.0.0.5), netstat shows no SMB/NFS/HTTP services listening—only the local resolver—so “file shares” would be inaccessible regardless of the client subnet, even though ICMP reaches the host. There is no evidence of a routing or interface fault in the network layer at this time.

Root cause: Not a routing problem; server-side services for the “file shares” are not running or not listening (at least on 1.0.0.5).

Corrective fix: Do not alter routing. Verify the exact server(s) users target (hostname/IP) and ensure the required services (e.g., SMB/NFS/HTTP) are up and listening on the Server Room hosts; restart or remediate those services. If the outage was intermittent, review server/application logs; RIP adjacencies are currently stable.

The agent's log contains multiple successful pings from CS hosts to 1.0.0.5 and a netstat from pc1 showing no service listeners; frr route checks were run (outputs truncated but present). The conclusion that routing is healthy and the problem is server-side (services not running) follows logically and covers the necessary checks to rule out routing faults.
